record.content_text:
The properties of a cone are:

- A cone has two *faces*. One of the faces is flat and the other face is curved.
- The *base* of a cone is a flat circle.
- [Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-039.png]
- A cone has only one side face, and this face is curved.
- Draw a circle and cut it out. Then cut out a "slice" (a sector) of the circle as shown below.
- [Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-040.png]
- Curl the paper around so that $AB$ fits onto $AC$. You are now holding the curved face of a cone in your hand. Although this face is curved, it can be laid flat, so it is still a face.
- A cone has only one *edge*. The edge of a cone is not a straight line; it is a curve.
- [Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-041.png]
- The edge of a cone is the circumference of the circle that forms the base of the cone.
- A cone has only one *vertex*.
- The vertex of a cone is at the top of the cone.
- [Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-042.png]

The one vertex of a cone is also called the *apex* of the cone. From the base, the curved face becomes narrower until it forms a point at the top, which is the apex.

record.evidence_quote: **cone** A cone is a 3D object with a circle as its base. A cone has one curved side face that comes to a point, the apex.
record.content_text: **cone** A cone is a 3D object with a circle as its base. A cone has one curved side face that comes to a point, the apex.

record.prompt_text:
Consider the diagram of the cone given below.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-043.png]

1. What is the name of the shaded area labelled $X$?
2. What shape is the shaded area labelled $X$?
3. Is the edge of a cone a straight line or a curve?
4. What is the name of the point labelled $Y$?
record.answer_text:
1. What is the name of the shaded area labelled $X$?

Step 1: Recall the properties of a cone.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-044.png]

A cone has a circle as its base. It has only one curved side face that narrows until it forms a point at the top, which is the apex.

Step 2: Identify the shaded area and give the correct answer.

The shaded area labelled $X$ is the base of the cone.

2. What shape is the shaded area labelled $X$?

Step 1: Recall the properties of a cone.

A cone has a circle as its base.

Step 2: Identify the shape and give the correct answer.

The base of the cone, labelled $X$, is a circle.

3. Is the edge of a cone a straight line or a curve?

Step 1: Recall the properties of a cone.

A cone has a circle as its base. It has only one curved side face that tapers to a single point at the apex.

Step 2: Identify the edge of the cone and give the correct answer.

The edge of a cone is curved. The edge of a cone is the circumference of the circle that is the base of the cone.

4. What is the name of the point labelled $Y$?

Step 1: Recall the properties of a cone.

A cone has a circle as its base. It has only one curved side face that tapers to a single point at the apex.

Step 2: Identify the point labelled $Y$ and give the correct answer.

The point $Y$ is the vertex of the cone. It is also called the apex of the cone.
